name: copy_sixteen_longs_then_call
description: Copies sixteen 32-bit values from a fixed offset of a base register into a buffer whose pointer is passed on the stack, then jumps through a code pointer held in a register. The caller is find_max_and_prepare_buffer.

name: run_with_conditional_task_setup
description: Clears a flag byte, looks up a task structure through a table-indirect call, and if its field at offset 172 is zero runs two setup routines and records a flag. It then calls the other routine and, when the flag is set, runs two cleanup routines before returning that routine's result.

name: poll_input_and_dispatch_loop
description: Initializes several global counters, buffers and mode flags, then loops without returning, polling an input routine and comparing the result with the character codes for the digits one to five and a fixed counter limit. Each pass advances a 32-bit counter and calls a sequence of other routines, some of them only when a bit flag is set.

name: allocate_table_slot
description: Checks the slot at the running counter's index in a small byte table; if the slot is empty and the counter is below 248, it stores the counter in the slot and in a paired word, advances the counter by four and returns the counter value. Otherwise it returns the slot's existing byte.

name: append_table_entry_if_space
description: When the running counter is below 248, writes its low byte into an indexed byte table and stores a two-word record at the counter's offset, then advances the counter by four. It does nothing when the table is full.

name: store_table_record_and_advance
description: Writes one byte into an indexed table and a two-word record at an offset from a pointer, then increments the 16-bit value at that pointer by four. It is the shared store step for the table-filling code and has three callers.

name: bucket_sort_four_byte_records
description: Sorts four-byte records in place by successive key fields, splitting each range into buckets with an explicit stack of pending ranges and a key mask that changes between passes. Afterwards it writes each bucket's start offset into an index table.

name: calculate_data_bounds
description: Sets six bounds to minus one, then scans a block of 16-bit words, splitting each into a low nibble, a middle nibble and a high byte, and tracks the minimum and maximum of each field. It stores each field's range and the sum of the three ranges in the structure.

name: clear_shifted_plane_block
description: Clears bits in four interleaved bitplanes over eight rows by ANDing each row with the complement of a source byte shifted by a signed amount taken from a register. For negative shifts that pass a bound check it also clears a second column of words in each row.

name: clear_shifted_plane_rows
description: Clears bits in four interleaved bitplanes over eight rows, with the source pointer, destination pointer and shift amount passed in registers. Each row is ANDed with the complement of the shifted source byte, and a second column is cleared when a bound check passes.

name: clear_plane_column_bits
description: Clears the bits of a shifted source byte from four interleaved bitplanes over a counted number of rows, advancing 20 words per row. The shift amount comes from a register and no second column is written.

name: write_colour_one_block
description: Writes colour index one into eight rows of four interleaved bitplanes: the first plane is set and the other three are cleared, using a shifted source byte. A second column of words receives the overflow bits in the same pattern when a bound check passes.

name: write_colour_one_rows
description: Same colour-one pattern as its wrapper over eight rows, with the destination, source and shift passed in registers. The first plane is ORed with the shifted byte and the other three planes are ANDed with its complement, plus a second column when a bound check passes.

name: write_colour_one_column
description: Writes colour index one into a counted number of rows of a single column across four bitplanes, advancing 20 words per row. The first plane is set and the other three are cleared, with the shift amount taken from a register.

name: write_colour_two_block
description: Writes colour index two over eight rows of four interleaved bitplanes, setting the second plane and clearing the other three from a shifted source byte. A second column receives the overflow bits in the same pattern when a bound check passes.

name: write_colour_two_rows
description: Same colour-two pattern as its wrapper over eight rows, with the destination, source and shift passed in registers. The second plane is ORed with the shifted byte while the others are ANDed with its complement, plus a second column when a bound check passes.

name: write_colour_two_column
description: Writes colour index two into a counted number of rows of a single column across four bitplanes, advancing 20 words per row. The second plane is set, the others are cleared, and the shift amount comes from a register.

name: write_colour_three_block
description: Writes colour index three over eight rows of four interleaved bitplanes, setting the first two planes and clearing the other two from a shifted source byte. A second column receives the overflow bits in the same pattern when a bound check passes.

name: write_colour_three_rows
description: Same colour-three pattern as its wrapper over eight rows, with the destination, source and shift passed in registers. The first two planes are ORed with the shifted byte and the last two are ANDed with its complement, plus a second column when a bound check passes.

name: write_colour_three_column
description: Writes colour index three into a counted number of rows of a single column across four bitplanes, advancing 20 words per row. The first two planes are set, the last two are cleared, and the shift amount comes from a register.

name: write_colour_four_block
description: Writes colour index four over eight rows of four interleaved bitplanes: only the third plane is set and the others are cleared, using a shifted source byte. A second column receives the overflow bits in the same pattern when a bound check passes.

name: write_colour_four_rows
description: Same colour-four pattern as its wrapper over eight rows, with the destination, source and shift passed in registers. Only the third plane is ORed with the shifted byte, and the other planes are ANDed with its complement, plus a second column when a bound check passes.

name: write_colour_four_column
description: Writes colour index four into a counted number of rows of a single column across four bitplanes, advancing 20 words per row. Only the third plane is set and the shift amount comes from a register.

name: write_colour_five_block
description: Writes colour index five over eight rows of four interleaved bitplanes, setting the first and third planes and clearing the second and fourth from a shifted source byte. A second column receives the overflow bits in the same pattern when a bound check passes.

name: write_colour_five_rows
description: Same colour-five pattern as its wrapper over eight rows, with the destination, source and shift passed in registers. The first and third planes are ORed with the shifted byte and the others are ANDed with its complement, plus a second column when a bound check passes.

name: write_colour_five_column
description: Writes colour index five into a counted number of rows of a single column across four bitplanes, advancing 20 words per row. The first and third planes are set, the second and fourth are cleared, and the shift amount comes from a register.

name: write_colour_six_block
description: Writes colour index six over eight rows of four interleaved bitplanes, setting the second and third planes and clearing the first and fourth from a shifted source byte. A second column receives the overflow bits in the same pattern when a bound check passes.

name: write_colour_six_rows
description: Same colour-six pattern as its wrapper over eight rows, with the destination, source and shift passed in registers. The second and third planes are ORed with the shifted byte and the others are ANDed with its complement, plus a second column when a bound check passes.

name: write_colour_six_column
description: Writes colour index six into a counted number of rows of a single column across four bitplanes, advancing 20 words per row. The second and third planes are set, the first and fourth are cleared, and the shift amount comes from a register.

name: write_colour_seven_block
description: Writes colour index seven over eight rows of four interleaved bitplanes, setting the first three planes and clearing the fourth from a shifted source byte. A second column receives the overflow bits in the same pattern when a bound check passes.

name: write_colour_seven_rows
description: Same colour-seven pattern as its wrapper over eight rows, with the destination, source and shift passed in registers. The first three planes are ORed with the shifted byte and the fourth is ANDed with its complement, plus a second column when a bound check passes.

name: write_colour_seven_column
description: Writes colour index seven into a counted number of rows of a single column across four bitplanes, advancing 20 words per row. The first three planes are set, the fourth is cleared, and the shift amount comes from a register.

name: write_colour_eight_block
description: Writes colour index eight over eight rows of four interleaved bitplanes: only the fourth plane is set and the others are cleared, using a shifted source byte. A second column receives the overflow bits in the same pattern when a bound check passes.

name: write_colour_eight_rows
description: Same colour-eight pattern as its wrapper over eight rows, with the destination, source and shift passed in registers. Only the fourth plane is ORed with the shifted byte, and the other planes are ANDed with its complement, plus a second column when a bound check passes.

name: write_colour_eight_column
description: Writes colour index eight into a counted number of rows of a single column across four bitplanes, advancing 20 words per row. Only the fourth plane is set and the shift amount comes from a register.

name: write_colour_nine_block
description: Writes colour index nine over eight rows of four interleaved bitplanes, setting the first and fourth planes and clearing the second and third from a shifted source byte. A second column receives the overflow bits in the same pattern when a bound check passes.

name: write_colour_nine_rows
description: Same colour-nine pattern as its wrapper over eight rows, with the destination, source and shift passed in registers. The first and fourth planes are ORed with the shifted byte and the middle two are ANDed with its complement, plus a second column when a bound check passes.

name: write_colour_nine_column
description: Writes colour index nine into a counted number of rows of a single column across four bitplanes, advancing 20 words per row. The first and fourth planes are set, the middle two are cleared, and the shift amount comes from a register.

name: write_colour_ten_block
description: Writes colour index ten over eight rows of four interleaved bitplanes, setting the second and fourth planes and clearing the first and third from a shifted source byte. A second column receives the overflow bits in the same pattern when a bound check passes.

name: write_colour_ten_rows
description: Same colour-ten pattern as its wrapper over eight rows, with the destination, source and shift passed in registers. The second and fourth planes are ORed with the shifted byte and the others are ANDed with its complement, plus a second column when a bound check passes.

name: write_colour_ten_column
description: Writes colour index ten into a counted number of rows of a single column across four bitplanes, advancing 20 words per row. The second and fourth planes are set, the first and third are cleared, and the shift amount comes from a register.

name: write_colour_eleven_block
description: Writes colour index eleven over eight rows of four interleaved bitplanes, setting the first, second and fourth planes and clearing the third from a shifted source byte. A second column receives the overflow bits in the same pattern when a bound check passes.

name: write_colour_eleven_rows
description: Same colour-eleven pattern as its wrapper over eight rows, with the destination, source and shift passed in registers. The first, second and fourth planes are ORed with the shifted byte and the third is ANDed with its complement, plus a second column when a bound check passes.

name: write_colour_eleven_column
description: Writes colour index eleven into a counted number of rows of a single column across four bitplanes, advancing 20 words per row. The first, second and fourth planes are set, the third is cleared, and the shift amount comes from a register.

name: write_colour_twelve_block
description: Writes colour index twelve over eight rows of four interleaved bitplanes, setting the third and fourth planes and clearing the first and second from a shifted source byte. A second column receives the overflow bits in the same pattern when a bound check passes.

name: write_colour_twelve_rows
description: Same colour-twelve pattern as its wrapper over eight rows, with the destination, source and shift passed in registers. The third and fourth planes are ORed with the shifted byte and the first two are ANDed with its complement, plus a second column when a bound check passes.

name: write_colour_twelve_column
description: Writes colour index twelve into a counted number of rows of a single column across four bitplanes, advancing 20 words per row. The third and fourth planes are set, the first and second are cleared, and the shift amount comes from a register.

name: write_colour_thirteen_block
description: Writes colour index thirteen over eight rows of four interleaved bitplanes, setting the first, third and fourth planes and clearing the second from a shifted source byte. A second column receives the overflow bits in the same pattern when a bound check passes.

name: write_colour_thirteen_rows
description: Same colour-thirteen pattern as its wrapper over eight rows, with the destination, source and shift passed in registers. The first, third and fourth planes are ORed with the shifted byte and the second is ANDed with its complement, plus a second column when a bound check passes.

name: write_colour_thirteen_column
description: Writes colour index thirteen into a counted number of rows of a single column across four bitplanes, advancing 20 words per row. The first, third and fourth planes are set, the second is cleared, and the shift amount comes from a register.

name: write_colour_fourteen_block
description: Writes colour index fourteen over eight rows of four interleaved bitplanes: the first plane is cleared and the other three are set, using a shifted source byte. A second column receives the overflow bits in the same pattern when a bound check passes.

name: write_colour_fourteen_rows
description: Same colour-fourteen pattern as its wrapper over eight rows, with the destination, source and shift passed in registers. The first plane is ANDed with the complement of the shifted byte and the other three are ORed with it, plus a second column when a bound check passes.

name: write_colour_fourteen_column
description: Writes colour index fourteen into a counted number of rows of a single column across four bitplanes, advancing 20 words per row. The first plane is cleared, the other three are set, and the shift amount comes from a register.

name: write_colour_fifteen_block
description: Writes colour index fifteen over eight rows of four interleaved bitplanes, setting all four planes from a shifted source byte. A second column receives the overflow bits in the same pattern when a bound check passes.

name: write_colour_fifteen_rows
description: Same colour-fifteen pattern as its wrapper over eight rows, with the destination, source and shift passed in registers. All four planes are ORed with the shifted byte, plus a second column when a bound check passes.

name: write_colour_fifteen_column
description: Writes colour index fifteen into a counted number of rows of a single column across four bitplanes, advancing 20 words per row. All four planes are set and the shift amount comes from a register.

name: post_request_block_when_idle
description: Waits until a status word at a fixed offset from a base register reads zero, then fills a request block: a byte of value 14, a word of value 10772, a pending marker of minus one, a long pointer loaded from a data address, and the words zero, four and minus one. It returns without waiting for the request to complete.

name: fill_request_block_no_wait
description: Fills the request block's pending marker, pointer, and the words zero, four and minus one without first waiting for the status word to clear. It writes no byte or constant at the other two offsets.

name: submit_request_and_wait
description: Calls the request-filling routine and then waits until the status word at the base register's fixed offset reads zero before returning.

name: reset_request_and_wait
description: Waits for the status word to read zero, writes the constant 10772 and a zero byte to two request locations, calls the request-filling routine, and waits for the status word to return to zero before returning.

name: reset_request_alt_and_wait
description: Waits for the status word to read zero, writes the constant 12820 and a zero byte to two request locations, calls the request-filling routine, and waits for the status word to return to zero before returning.

name: call_pointer_at_base
description: Calls the code pointer stored in the first longword at the address held in the base register and returns. It is reached from two other routines.

name: call_four_routines_in_order
description: Calls four routines one after another with no other work of its own, then returns.

name: layout_text_from_table_entry
description: Stores a pointer taken from a global table and a position word into the output block, then, if the line counter is below 192, parses a byte stream until a zero byte. Bytes at or above 32 are printed through a routine while the x position is below 316; the control codes 1, 13 and 30 respectively load a table entry, advance the line counter by ten, and set x to twice the next byte.

name: start_text_layout_with_routine
description: Stores the address of a fixed routine and a width taken as twice the first stream byte into the output block, then reads a line limit from the next byte. If the line counter is below 192 it parses the rest of the byte stream using the same control codes and printing rules.

name: resume_text_layout
description: Stores the position word into the output block and, if the line counter is below 192, parses the byte stream from the current position until a zero byte. It uses the same control codes and printing limits as its siblings.

name: parse_text_control_codes
description: Main loop of a byte-stream text parser: bytes at or above 32 are printed through a routine while x stays below 316, and the control codes 1, 13 and 30 are dispatched to their handlers. The loop returns on a zero byte or when the line counter reaches 192.

name: start_text_run_at_width
description: Sets x from twice the first stream byte and then parses the rest of the byte stream with the usual text control codes, returning on a zero byte or when the line counter reaches 192.

name: dispatch_text_control_code
description: Handles the control codes of the text parser: code 13 advances the line counter by ten and returns at 192, code 1 loads a table entry from the next byte, and other codes continue to the printing loop.

name: advance_text_line_and_parse
description: Adds ten to the line counter, returns if it has reached 192, and otherwise resumes printing the byte stream at the current x position using the text control codes.

name: store_entry_and_skip_string
description: When the line counter is below 192, stores a table entry pointer and a position word into the output block, then advances the string pointer to the zero byte that ends the string.

name: skip_text_stream_arguments
description: Walks a zero-terminated byte stream, stepping over the argument bytes that follow each control code; control code 1 also loads a table entry from the byte it steps over. It returns at the zero terminator.

name: advance_to_next_zero_byte
description: Advances a string pointer by at least one byte and keeps going until it reaches the next zero byte, which it leaves the pointer on.

name: load_entries_from_text_stream
description: Walks a zero-terminated byte stream and, for each control code 1 it meets, loads a table entry from the byte after it. The loop ends at the zero terminator.

name: find_end_of_string
description: Advances a pointer while the byte at it is nonzero and stops on the zero terminator. It does no other work.

name: sort_four_values_network
description: Puts four 16-bit values in order with a compare-and-swap sequence, then computes differences between the ordered values. The routine is reached only from decoded gap bytes, so no normal caller is known.

name: compute_fixed_point_slope
description: Computes a fixed-point slope from two 16-bit differences by shifting one difference left by eight bits and dividing by the other, handling a zero divisor separately. It stores a sign flag in a global variable and returns the scaled result. Its entry is marked unreached in the listing, and the callers are unnamed routines.

name: compute_slope_start_position
description: Computes a start position and a fixed-point slope from two 16-bit differences using the same divide-by-difference scheme, and stores a sign flag in a global variable. Its entry is marked unreached in the listing, and the callers are unnamed routines.

name: walk_edges_calling_span_routine
description: Steps two fixed-point edge accumulators for a counted number of iterations and calls a span routine through a jump table whenever the integer width between them is below 321. Its entry is marked unreached in the listing, and the callers are unnamed routines.

name: step_edges_and_call_span
description: Variant of its neighbour that starts from a different register set: it steps two fixed-point edge accumulators and calls the span routine through a jump table for each width below 321. Its entry is marked unreached in the listing, and the callers are unnamed routines.

name: walk_edge_pair_spans
description: Steps two fixed-point edge accumulators by per-iteration deltas over a counted loop and calls a span routine through a jump table whenever the integer width between them is below 321. Its entry is marked unreached in the listing, and the callers are unnamed routines.

name: start_edge_pair_walk
description: Orders two fixed-point starting positions, stores a sign flag in a global variable, and runs a counted loop that steps the accumulators and calls the span routine through a jump table for widths below 321. Its entry is marked unreached in the listing.

name: start_edge_walk_shifted
description: Variant of its neighbour that builds the starting positions from shifted 16-bit values before ordering them, sets the sign flag, and runs the same counted span loop for widths below 321. Its entry is marked unreached in the listing.

name: walk_single_edge_spans
description: Steps one fixed-point edge accumulator and a second accumulator over a counted loop, calling the span routine through a jump table for each integer width below 321, then returns. Its entry is marked unreached in the listing and it has one unnamed caller.

name: scan_convert_edge_list
description: Reads an entry from a global table at an index held in a register, orders coordinate pairs, and computes fixed-point steps by dividing one difference by another in a loop, calling a routine on each pass. It is entered through a handler pointer stored in data.

name: compute_edge_step_fixed
description: Computes the differences between two coordinate pairs, divides the x difference by the y difference with eight-bit fixed-point scaling, and returns the step value, with a separate branch for a zero divisor. Its entry is marked unreached in the listing.

name: compute_edge_step_swapped
description: Computes the same fixed-point step as its neighbour with the start position swapped into the high word first, stores a sign flag in a global variable, and returns the step. Its entry is marked unreached in the listing.

name: compute_edge_start_and_step
description: Builds a fixed-point start position from a 16-bit value, computes the difference-divided step between two coordinate pairs, and stores a sign flag in a global variable. It is reached through a data pointer and its callers are unnamed routines.

name: order_span_bounds_and_step
description: Compares two 16-bit values, orders two span bounds, stores a sign flag in a global variable, and steps the edge accumulators over the resulting range. It is reached through a data pointer and its callers are unnamed routines.

name: order_span_bounds_with_start
description: Orders two span bounds derived from a start position and a step, stores a sign flag in a global variable, and steps the accumulators with the same handling. It is reached through a data pointer and its callers are unnamed routines.

name: walk_edges_then_compute_step
description: Walks two fixed-point edge accumulators over a counted loop, calling a span routine through a jump table for each integer width below 321, then computes a fixed-point step by dividing the x difference of two stacked point pairs by their y difference. It is reached through a data pointer; its caller is an unnamed routine.

name: walk_edge_spans_if_fits
description: Runs the edge-walking span loop only when a count is no greater than the difference of two 16-bit values, calling the span routine through a jump table for widths below 321. It stores a sign flag in a global variable and is reached through a data pointer.

name: walk_edge_spans_from_offset
description: Builds its starting accumulator from a 16-bit value offset by a fixed amount, then runs the counted span loop with a jump-table call for widths below 321 and stores a sign flag. Its two callers are unnamed routines.

name: walk_edges_then_divide_pair
description: Runs the counted span loop with a jump-table call for widths below 321, then computes a fixed-point step by dividing the x difference of two stack-passed values by their y difference. Its caller is an unnamed routine.

name: walk_edge_spans_only
description: Steps two fixed-point edge accumulators over a counted loop, calling the span routine through a jump table for each width below 321, and returns with no further work. Its caller is an unnamed routine.

name: walk_edge_spans_ordered
description: Orders two starting accumulators by a sign flag, runs the counted span loop with a jump-table call for widths below 321, and returns. Its two callers are unnamed routines.

name: walk_edge_spans_simple
description: Runs a counted span loop that steps two accumulators and calls the span routine through a jump table for widths below 321, without ordering or step computation. Its caller is an unnamed routine.

name: walk_edges_then_update_pair
description: Runs the counted span loop with a jump-table call for widths below 321, then subtracts two stack-passed values from a stored pair and stores the sign-dependent result. Its caller is an unnamed routine.

name: walk_then_divide_offset_pair
description: Runs the counted span loop with a jump-table call for widths below 321, then subtracts stack-passed offsets from a pair and computes a fixed-point step by dividing the x difference by the y difference. Its caller is an unnamed routine.

name: walk_edge_spans_swapped
description: Orders the two starting accumulators by a sign flag, then runs the counted span loop with a jump-table call for widths below 321 and returns. Its caller is an unnamed routine.

name: walk_edge_spans_start_word
description: Sets its starting accumulator from a 16-bit value, stores a sign flag in a global variable, and runs a counted loop that calls the span routine through a jump table for widths below 321. Its two callers are unnamed routines.

name: walk_edge_spans_minus_half
description: Runs a counted span loop that steps two accumulators, with the first starting point offset by minus 32768, and calls the span routine through a jump table for widths below 321. Its caller is an unnamed routine.

name: walk_edge_spans_then_swap
description: Runs the counted span loop with a jump-table call for widths below 321, then orders the two accumulators by the sign flag and stores the result. Its caller is an unnamed routine.

name: walk_then_divide_stack_offset
description: Runs the counted span loop with a jump-table call for widths below 321, then computes a fixed-point step by dividing the x difference of stack-passed values by their y difference. Its caller is an unnamed routine.

name: walk_spans_if_count_fits
description: Runs the counted span loop only when a count is no greater than the difference of two 16-bit values, calling the span routine through a jump table for widths below 321. It stores a sign flag and is reached through a data pointer.

name: walk_edge_spans_gated_start
description: Builds its starting accumulators from a 16-bit value and, when a count fits the difference of two words, runs the counted span loop with a jump-table call for widths below 321. Its two callers are unnamed routines.

name: walk_then_divide_param_pair
description: Runs the counted span loop with a jump-table call for widths below 321, then subtracts a stack-passed pair from another and computes a fixed-point step by dividing the x difference by the y difference. Its caller is an unnamed routine.

name: walk_edge_spans_unordered
description: Runs a counted loop that steps two accumulators, calling the span routine through a jump table for each integer width below 321, and returns without ordering or computing a step. Its caller is an unnamed routine.

name: walk_edge_spans_from_word
description: Sets its starting accumulator from a 16-bit value, stores a sign flag in a global variable, and runs a counted span loop with a jump-table call for widths below 321 before returning.

name: walk_edge_spans_minimal
description: Steps two accumulators over a counted loop and calls the span routine through a jump table for each width below 321, then returns. Its caller is an unnamed routine.

name: walk_edge_spans_flagged
description: Runs a counted span loop that steps two accumulators and calls the span routine through a jump table for widths below 321, then orders the accumulators by a sign flag stored in a global variable. It is reached through a data pointer.

name: walk_edges_then_divide_relative
description: Runs the counted span loop with a jump-table call for widths below 321, then computes a fixed-point step by dividing the x difference of two stacked values by their y difference. Its caller is an unnamed routine.

name: walk_edge_spans_with_count
description: Runs a counted span loop that steps two accumulators and calls the span routine through a jump table for widths below 321, with the count taken from a register. Its caller is an unnamed routine.

name: walk_edge_spans_offset_word
description: Sets its starting accumulator from a 16-bit value offset by a fixed amount, then runs a counted span loop with a jump-table call for widths below 321. Its two callers are unnamed routines.

name: walk_edge_spans_short_count
description: Steps two accumulators over a short counter, calling the span routine through a jump table for each width below 321, and returns. Its caller is an unnamed routine.

name: dispatch_indexed_routine_in_bounds
description: Returns unless two register values lie within 2 to 317 and 2 to 165. Otherwise it calls one of several routines selected by a small index, each found through a 16-bit offset stored in the table the argument points to; one index path calls an empty stub that returns immediately.

name: call_table_routine_at_four
description: Calls the routine whose 16-bit offset is stored at byte four of the table pointed to by its argument, then returns.

name: call_table_routine_at_six
description: Calls the routine whose 16-bit offset is stored at byte six of the table pointed to by its argument, then returns.

name: call_table_routine_six_variant
description: Calls the routine whose 16-bit offset is stored at byte six of the table pointed to by its argument, then returns. It is the same call as its neighbour, kept as a separate entry.

name: call_table_routine_at_eight
description: Calls the routine whose 16-bit offset is stored at byte eight of the table pointed to by its argument, then returns.

name: stub_return_only
description: Contains only a return, with no calls, memory access or hardware register use, so it performs no work.

name: dispatch_indexed_routine_buffered
description: Reads a table pointer from a global variable, bounds-checks two register values against 2 to 317 and 2 to 165, then dispatches by an index below six through 16-bit table offsets. Larger indices reserve a local buffer of 2016 words and call further routines.

name: fill_edge_tables_both_ends
description: Loops writing word pairs built from a row value and a 16-bit value into two tables that grow from opposite ends, switching sides by the sign of a counter. The loop ends when its count is exhausted.

name: draw_clipped_span_list
description: Walks a list of word pairs, clamping a limit to 168 and skipping pairs whose adjusted span is not within 0 to 320. For each remaining span it calls a routine through a jump table.

name: fill_edge_pair_table_step
description: Writes word pairs into two tables that grow from opposite ends and advances the counters by fixed steps on each pass, calling one routine per pass. Its caller is an unnamed routine.

name: step_line_pixels_with_error
description: Takes the absolute x and y deltas between two points and steps along the major axis with a fixed-point error term, calling a routine selected from a table for each step. It returns the remaining step count.

name: step_line_pixels_with_status
description: Steps a line with the same error-term arithmetic as its neighbours, calling a table routine for each step, and returns -1 when the step count runs out; otherwise it returns the count. It has four unnamed callers.

name: run_table_routine_sequence
description: Counts down a step count, calling the routine at the current index of a table for each step while advancing an accumulator, and calls one more table entry when the count reaches zero. It has two unnamed callers.

name: step_table_routine_accumulator
description: Starts from a count derived from a register and calls the first table routine in a loop while adjusting a fixed-point accumulator, returning the remaining count.

name: step_line_pixels_unreached
description: Counts steps along a line with the same error-term loop as its neighbours, calling a table routine for each step and returning the remaining count. Its entry is marked unreached in the listing, and it has three unnamed callers.

name: run_table_routine_sequence_second
description: Same counted table-routine sequence as its sibling: it calls the routine at the current table index for each step while advancing an accumulator, and calls one more table entry on completion. It has two unnamed callers.

name: step_table_routine_second
description: Repeats the accumulator loop of its sibling: it steps a fixed-point accumulator over a count, calling the first table routine per step and returning the remaining count. Its caller is an unnamed routine.

name: step_line_table_routines
description: Computes two differences from its arguments, sets an error term from a negated start value, and steps along the major axis, calling a table routine for each step. It returns the remaining step count and has three unnamed callers.

name: run_table_routine_sequence_third
description: Same counted table-routine sequence as its siblings, calling the routine at the current table index for each step and one more entry on completion. Its caller is an unnamed routine.

name: step_table_routine_third
description: Repeats the accumulator loop of its siblings: it steps a fixed-point accumulator over a count, calling the first table routine per step and returning the remaining count. Its caller is an unnamed routine.

name: step_line_table_routines_alt
description: Steps along the major axis of a line with an error term, using the other branch of the difference comparison, and calls a table routine for each step. Its entry is marked unreached in the listing and it has three unnamed callers.

name: run_table_routine_sequence_fourth
description: Same counted table-routine sequence as its siblings, calling the routine at the current table index for each step and one more entry on completion. It has two unnamed callers.

name: step_table_routine_fourth
description: Repeats the accumulator loop of its siblings: it steps a fixed-point accumulator over a count, calling the first table routine per step and returning the remaining count. Its caller is an unnamed routine.

name: step_two_edges_in_screen
description: Steps four fixed-point accumulators per iteration, one pair per edge. While both coordinates stay within 0 to 319 and 0 to 167 it calls a routine to plot, and it stops when a coordinate leaves that range. Its entry is marked unreached in the listing.

name: step_two_edges_plot_pair
description: Steps four fixed-point accumulators per iteration, and while both coordinates lie within 0 to 319 and 0 to 167 it calls a routine twice. It loops on a counter passed on the stack. Its entry is marked unreached in the listing, and it has one unnamed caller.

name: step_two_edges_counted_loop
description: Steps four fixed-point accumulators per iteration, calling a routine twice per pass while the coordinates stay on screen, and loops on a counter passed on the stack. Its entry is marked unreached in the listing and it has one unnamed caller.

name: stub_return_immediately
description: Contains only a return, so it does nothing. It has two unnamed callers.

name: call_routine_four_times
description: Calls the same routine four times in succession and returns.

name: draw_clipped_sprite_planes
description: Rejects a sprite record whose position is negative or whose extent passes 320 horizontally or 168 vertically. Otherwise it draws the record into bitplanes, shifting the data by the low four bits of the x position when that position is not word-aligned, and calling other routines for each plane write. It is reached through a data pointer.

name: draw_clipped_sprite_wide
description: Same sprite drawing as its neighbour, but it clips the height against 200 instead of 168. It is reached through a data pointer and has two unnamed callers.

name: copy_column_to_bitplanes
description: Copies longwords from a source buffer into a destination with a stride of ten longwords, then writes the same values to a second bitplane offset 8000 bytes away. The first copy runs only when a status flag from the caller is set.

name: call_table_handler_four_sides
description: When its index is not 18, loads a routine pointer from a table at that index and calls it along the four counted sides of a rectangle. Index 18 takes a separate branch that is not described here.

name: call_table_handler_frame
description: Loads a routine pointer from a table at its index and calls it along the four counted sides of a rectangle, using the same loops as its neighbour without a special index. Its caller is an unnamed routine.

name: copy_long_and_word
description: Copies one longword and the word that follows it from one buffer to another, then returns.

name: copy_two_longs
description: Copies two consecutive longwords from one buffer to another, then returns.

name: copy_five_words
description: Copies five 16-bit words from a source pointer to a destination pointer, then returns. It is reached through a pointer in data.

name: copy_three_longs
description: Copies three 32-bit words from a source pointer to a destination pointer, then returns. It is reached through a pointer in data.

name: copy_seven_words
description: Copies seven 16-bit words from a source pointer to a destination pointer, then returns. It is reached through a pointer in data.

name: copy_four_longs
description: Copies four 32-bit words from a source pointer to a destination pointer, then returns. It is reached through a pointer in data.

name: copy_nine_words
description: Copies nine 16-bit words from a source pointer to a destination pointer, then returns. It is reached through a pointer in data.

name: copy_five_longs
description: Copies five 32-bit words from a source pointer to a destination pointer, then returns. It is reached through a pointer in data.

name: copy_five_longs_and_word
description: Copies five 32-bit words and one following 16-bit word from a source pointer to a destination pointer, then returns. It is reached through a pointer in data.

name: copy_six_longs
description: Copies six 32-bit words from a source pointer to a destination pointer, then returns. It is reached through a pointer in data.

name: copy_six_longs_and_word
description: Copies six 32-bit words and one following 16-bit word from a source pointer to a destination pointer, then returns. It is reached through a pointer in data.

name: copy_seven_longs
description: Copies seven 32-bit words from a source pointer to a destination pointer, then returns. It is reached through a pointer in data.

name: copy_seven_longs_and_word
description: Copies seven 32-bit words and one following 16-bit word from a source pointer to a destination pointer, then returns. It is reached through a pointer in data.

name: copy_eight_longs
description: Copies eight 32-bit words from a source pointer to a destination pointer, then returns. It is reached through a pointer in data.

name: copy_eight_longs_and_word
description: Copies eight 32-bit words and one following 16-bit word from a source pointer to a destination pointer, then returns. It is reached through a pointer in data.

name: copy_nine_longs
description: Copies nine 32-bit words from a source pointer to a destination pointer, then returns. It is reached through a pointer in data.

name: copy_nine_longs_and_word
description: Copies nine 32-bit words and one following 16-bit word from a source pointer to a destination pointer, then returns. It is reached through a pointer in data.

name: draw_shifted_word_column
description: Draws a column of shifted 16-bit words from a record into bitplanes, merging each word with existing bits through masks derived from a position value. A record whose first word is 1 takes a branch that calls three routines before drawing. Its caller is an unnamed routine.

name: merge_shifted_words_column
description: Loops over a count of 16-bit words, shifting each word by a register amount and merging it into a bitplane column with a mask, advancing ten longwords per row. Its caller is an unnamed routine.

name: call_routine_four_times_alt
description: Calls the same routine four times in succession and returns. It is reached through a pointer in data and has one unnamed caller.

name: shift_word_grid_into_plane
description: Walks a two-dimensional array of 16-bit words, shifting each value by a register amount and merging it into a bitplane with a mask, advancing ten longwords between rows. Its caller is an unnamed routine.

name: stub_return_entry_point
description: Contains only a return, so it does nothing. It is reached through a pointer in data.

name: stub_return_no_work
description: Contains only a return, so it does nothing. It is reached through a pointer in data and has no callees.

name: shift_word_left_five
description: Returns its 16-bit register argument shifted left by five bits. It is reached through a pointer in data and has no callees.

name: xor_word_at_indexed_offset
description: Exclusive-ORs a 16-bit value into a word at a fixed offset from the base register plus twice an index. Its entry is marked unreached in the listing and it has no callees.

name: call_routine_over_rows
description: Returns after two calls when a count is negative. Otherwise it loops over a count of rows and, for each row, calls a routine found through a table pointer and a 16-bit offset, stopping when a secondary count reaches zero. It is reached through a pointer in data.

name: call_two_routines_in_order
description: Calls two routines in sequence and returns. Its caller is an unnamed routine.

name: call_handler_per_row_clamped
description: Clamps a count so that it plus a register value stays below 198, calls one routine when a low-nibble test on an argument passes, and then calls the routine stored at a fixed table offset once for each count value, including zero. It is reached through a pointer in data.

name: call_handler_per_row
description: Calls the routine stored at a fixed table offset once for each count value from a register, including zero, then returns. Its two callers are unnamed routines.

name: scale_product_to_range
description: Multiplies two 16-bit values by a count, forms a fixed-point product, and shifts it right until its value lies within plus or minus 7935, then returns the scaled value. It is reached through a pointer in data.

name: halve_pair_into_range
description: Halves the first 16-bit value, and the second along with it, until the first is at most 7935. It then halves the second value until its absolute value is at most 7935. Its caller is an unnamed routine.

name: halve_value_into_range
description: Halves a 16-bit register value until its absolute value is at most 7935, then returns. It is reached through a pointer in data and has two unnamed callers.

name: halve_value_positive_range
description: Halves a 16-bit register value until it is at most 7935. Negative values are not handled by this routine. It is reached through a pointer in data.

name: stub_return_called_twice
description: Contains only a return, so it does nothing. It has two unnamed callers.

name: scale_product_by_halving
description: Multiplies two 16-bit values by a register count, shifts the products down, and halves the results until they lie within plus or minus 7935. It returns a 32-bit scaled value. It is reached through a pointer in data.

name: halve_pair_into_range_alt
description: Same halving as its earlier sibling: it halves the first value, and the second along with it, until the first is at most 7935, then halves the second until its absolute value is at most 7935. Its caller is an unnamed routine.

name: halve_value_into_range_alt
description: Halves a 16-bit register value until its absolute value is at most 7935, then returns. It is reached through a pointer in data and has two unnamed callers.

name: halve_value_positive_alt
description: Halves a 16-bit register value until it is at most 7935, with no handling of negative values. Its caller is an unnamed routine.

name: stub_return_second_entry
description: Contains only a return, so it does nothing. It has two unnamed callers.

name: scale_three_values_magnitude
description: Shifts three values right by two until the first is within a 16-bit range, then computes the magnitude of the second relative to the third and returns it. It is reached through a pointer in data.

name: scale_three_values_second
description: Shifts three values right by two until the first is no longer below minus 32768, then computes the magnitude of the second relative to the third. Its caller is an unnamed routine.

name: scale_values_by_quarters
description: When the second value lies within the magnitude of the third, shifts the values right by two until the second fits within 32767. If the third then exceeds 16383, it shifts again until the third is at most 32767. It is reached through a pointer in data.

name: scale_pair_by_table_lookup
description: Shifts two values right until a count fits within 32767, then multiplies each value by a 16-bit entry from a global table selected by the shifted count, and returns both scaled values. It is reached through a pointer in data.

name: normalise_pair_for_clip
description: Compares a value with the magnitude of a second value and shifts both right by two when they are too large, then continues by calling other routines to finish the clip. Its caller is an unnamed routine.

name: scale_by_table_then_halve
description: Multiplies two 16-bit values by a table entry selected by a shifted index, shifts the products right, and halves them until the first lies within plus or minus 7935. Its caller is an unnamed routine.

name: scale_pair_by_table_shift
description: Multiplies two 16-bit values by a table entry selected by a shifted index and returns both products packed into one 64-bit value, each shifted right. It is reached through a pointer in data.

name: scale_pair_normalised_table
description: Shifts two values right until a count fits within 32767, then multiplies each value by a table entry selected by the shifted count and returns both products packed into one 64-bit value. It is reached through a pointer in data.

name: return_offset_or_minimum
description: If its argument exceeds 63, calls a routine and returns that result plus 160; otherwise it returns minus 32768. It is reached through a pointer in data and has two unnamed callers.

name: return_constant_half_range
description: Returns the 16-bit constant 32768. Its caller is an unnamed routine.

name: compute_three_component_magnitude
description: Takes the absolute values of three arguments, forms scaled products of their high words, and sums them into a fixed-point magnitude. It is reached through a pointer in data and has callers in two data hunks.

name: compute_fixed_point_square_root
description: Computes the square root of a 32-bit fixed-point value with an iterative bit-by-bit loop and returns the result in a 64-bit value. It is reached through a handler pointer in data and has one unnamed caller.

name: find_top_bit_of_half
description: Calls a routine for a value, halves the result, then doubles a candidate until it reaches the top bit of a 16-bit word, and returns the candidate masked to 15 bits. It is reached through a pointer in data and calls one unnamed routine.
